_prepare_database(registered): creates the table servers (ip, port, username, password, keyid) if it does not exist and stores the servers already registered. Columns without a declared type, because the original schema (dbinitalization.py) is not in the dataset; so SQLite stores the values as received.

run(registered, server): prepares the database, unpacks server (tuple of 5) in the call to the function of the snippet and returns the rows of the table.
Checked: Pysmell only flags the function of the snippet (PAR=5); nothing in the scaffolding.
pinned_behavior: typical: a common IP ('10.0.0.1') raises sqlite3.ProgrammingError, because the DELETE receives (ip), the string itself, and each character becomes a parameter (8 for 1 placeholder); nothing printed and the table stays the same.
edge: a one-character ip ('a') removes all rows with that ip, ignoring the other 4 arguments, and prints 'Server removed.'.
invalid: ip None raises sqlite3.ProgrammingError (parameters of an unsupported type); nothing printed and the table stays the same.
not_pinned_on_purpose: Connection left open when the DELETE fails: accidental side effect, not observable by the caller.
notes: Defect of the original pinned as it is (refactoring is not fixing bugs): with any real IP the function fails. A refactoring that replaces (ip) with (ip,) changes the behavior and fails the typical test.
port, username, password and keyid are not used by the snippet; removing these parameters is allowed, as long as run keeps the same signature.
